# guile

> guile is a lightweight Python framework for building desktop apps. It layers
> interactivity on top of ordinary Python: reactive state (`gui.state`) wires
> your existing functions to widgets, layout is written with `with` blocks, and
> the app runs as one Python process that opens a native window (pywebview /
> WebView2 / WKWebView). No server, no ports, no browser tab.

Install: `pip install guile` — requires Python >= 3.9. Current version: 0.8.7.

Every app follows the same five-part structure, in order: (1) your plain
Python functions, (2) `gui.state()` declarations at module level, (3) callbacks
that read `.value` and write with `.set()`, (4) a `ui()` function decorated
with `@gui.app()` that only reads state and builds layout, (5) `gui.run()` as
the last line. Code after `gui.run()` executes when the window closes.

Beyond widgets: `gui.leaflet()` maps take image/tile/GeoJSON overlays
(`layers=`) and Python-owned drawn areas (`drawn=` with edit/delete/click
callbacks); `gui.task()` runs slow work off the UI thread; `gui.package()`
builds a shareable executable (onedir by default).

## Docs

- [Complete AI reference (single file)](https://andpatrig.github.io/guile/llms-full.txt): full API, rules, and canonical examples — read this to write guile apps
- [How-to guide](https://andpatrig.github.io/guile/guile_howto.html): human-oriented tutorial with annotated examples
- [API reference](https://andpatrig.github.io/guile/guile_reference.html): human-oriented widget reference

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/andpatrig/guile): source, examples/ directory with 16 runnable apps, README
